messages.subject: High MVPA values using Roscoe et al. intensity thresholds
messages.subject_clean: High MVPA values using Roscoe et al. intensity thresholds
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm processing 24-hour data collected with the Axivity AX3 worn on the non-dominant wrist in children ages 3-5 using the Roscoe et al. intensity thresholds. Our data show very high values (~11 hours MVPA/day). Has anyone else experienced this? The code is listed below:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(
  mode=c(3:5),
  datadir=datadir",
  outputdir=outputdir,
  g.cwaread("D:/Axivity/Downloaded Files),

  do.report=c(2,4,5),
  do.enmoa = TRUE,
  do.enmo = FALSE,
  strategy = 2,
  includedaycrit = 16,
  windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
  winhr = c(5,10),
  qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
  qwindow=c(0,24),
  ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
  mvpathreshold =c(104),
  bout.metric = 6,
  overwrite= TRUE,
  epochvalues2csv= TRUE,
  #=====================
  # Part 3 + 4
  #=====================
  timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
  acc.metric="ENMOa",
  ignorenonwear = TRUE,
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  includenightcrit = 4,
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  outliers.only = TRUE,
  criterror = 4,
  relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
  do.visual = TRUE,

  #=====================
  # Part 5
  #=====================
  threshold.lig = c(61.8),
  threshold.mod = c(100.4),
  threshold.vig=(1004),
  boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(1), boutdur.lig = c(1),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1), save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE,
  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
  timewindow = c("WW"),
  visualreport=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Missing Data
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Missing Data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mohummed,

Part 5 facilitates 24/7 time-use analysis as needed for modern compositional analysis. For that we need a reliable estimate of sleep in the night starting a day and the night on which the day ends. Further, we cannot deal with half days of data because for time-use analysis an incomplete day can severely skew the results when aggregated across the measurement. Note that GGIR only estimates sleep on nights where at least midnight is part of the data, by which no sleep will be available for the last half night if the recording ends just before midnight.

GGIR tries to estimate when a person wake ups after the first midnight, but currently makes no effect to detect when the person goes to bed the last night because there is a chance that the person fell a sleep after the recording ended. Even if the person fell a sleep a few minutes before the end of the recording a reliable detection of this cannot be guaranteed. So, reliability of sleep assessment is potentially compromised for the last night. As a result, GGIR intentionally only uses 6 out of 7 days.

To assess a person 24/7 behaviour over a complete week your recordings should ideally last at least 9 days, and predominantly contain a high level of wear.

Seven day study protocols were traditionally used to only capture average acceleration per day and time spent in MVPA. However, with the modern interest in sedentary behaviour and compositional analysis, the 7-day protocol is out-dated. It simply is not sufficient to capture all the behaviours we are interested in.

On a related note - I am currently working on a project to modify this functionality a little bit such that if you really want you can include the 7th day. This may be useful for studies in children where we can assume a bit more safely that they fall a sleep before midnight. However, I will urge users to be careful with this as it is far from ideal and will make sure it is not a default setting.

Cheers,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Sarah,

Do I understand correctly that you see this consistently across the devices used in your study. If it would be one recording then I suspect something is wrong with the sensor calibration. What is the calibration error reported in part2_summary.csv? If it is consistent across your dataset then one possibility may be that Actigraph's idle sleep mode with zero string imputation is causes problems, because if there are only zeros and GGIR subtracts 1 and then takes the absolute (as is the case in ENMOa) you will get a consistent acceleration with magnitude of gravity during idle.sleep.mode periods.
Which form of raw data did you use?
.gt3x directly
.csv exported via Actilife
.csv exported in another way
Did you use GGIR 2.6-0 or high to process the data?

The threshold of 100.4 you specify does not sound too radical to me.

So, one thing you could try is to reprocess a few files with .gt3x data as input and with latest GGIR version 2.6-0 or higher.

Thanks,
Vincent

Hi all,

A survey I am working on is planning to use GGIR in analysing our accelerometer data being recorded on Axivity AX3 devices. Once in the field, we will have less accelerometers than respondents, so will need to extract then clear the data, before re-using the devices. We have established unique identifiers for each use of the accelerometer – for example, Accelerometer 1 is given code A the first time, code B for its second use, code C the third time, and so forth.  This is important as we will be using this unique identifier to link the individual respondents to other data they will be providing as part of the survey, e.g. age, sex, location. Hence, this identifier (rather than the accelerometer serial number) is vital for us to capture.

This identifier will be typed into the ‘Code’ field in the ‘Subject’ section in Open Movement, as seen in the image attached.

What I am unsure about is if there is a way to extract this information in GGIR. I assume it can be but then I am aware this R-package is used across multiple accelerometer brands that have different initialisation processes.

Any insight into how to output this information using GGIR would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards,
Nathaniel Sage

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to recalculate summary information (part2_summary.csv) after editing daysummary information (part2_daysummary.csv). Is there a way to edit information in the daysummary.csv file and have GGIR recalculate a summary.csv file?

Details:
I worked with participants in a small community, and lived in the community while conducting research. Participants wore an Activity AX3 accelerometer on the dominant wrist for one week. Most participants wore the accelerometer the full week, no problems. For these participants, I do not need to edit any daysummary information or recalculate summary information.

Some participants did not wear the accelerometer for the full week (did not wear the accelerometer at least 16 hours per day most days of the week), and I asked them to wear an accelerometer again, which they did. For these participants, I have two sets of daysummary and summary info that I’d like to combine (e.g., recalculate someone’s summary.csv data by combining data from the 2 valid days they wore an accelerometer the first week and the 5 valid days they wore an accelerometer the second week).

Other participants did not wear the accelerometer for the full week—either I observed or they informed me that they gave their accelerometer to a different person to wear on a particular day or days. So although their accelerometry data indicates that the accelerometer was worn for at least 16 hours per day throughout the week, I would like to be able to remove particular days from analysis.

In both of these cases, the best solution I’ve come up with is to manually recalculate summary information after editing the daysummary information. Is there a way I can have GGIR do this — so that the way the day summary information is used to calculate the values in the full summary is consistent?

Thank you for your help,
Katie

Hi Sarah,​

> calibration error in part 2 summary csv is consistently 0

What does QC_message in the column next to it say? Zero may mean that autocalibration was not attempted. Auto-calibration is usually difficult when accelerometer is hardly worn. Maybe try turning of autocalibration?

Vincent

On Mon, Apr 4, 2022, 5:14 PM Vincent van Hees <v.va...@accelting.com> wrote:
> Hi Mohummed,
>
> Part 5 facilitates 24/7 time-use analysis as needed for modern compositional analysis. For that we need a reliable estimate of sleep in the night starting a day and the night on which the day ends. Further, we cannot deal with half days of data because for time-use analysis an incomplete day can severely skew the results when aggregated across the measurement. Note that GGIR only estimates sleep on nights where at least midnight is part of the data, by which no sleep will be available for the last half night if the recording ends just before midnight.
>
> GGIR tries to estimate when a person wake ups after the first midnight, but currently makes no effect to detect when the person goes to bed the last night because there is a chance that the person fell a sleep after the recording ended. Even if the person fell a sleep a few minutes before the end of the recording a reliable detection of this cannot be guaranteed. So, reliability of sleep assessment is potentially compromised for the last night. As a result, GGIR intentionally only uses 6 out of 7 days.
>
> To assess a person 24/7 behaviour over a complete week your recordings should ideally last at least 9 days, and predominantly contain a high level of wear.
>
> Seven day study protocols were traditionally used to only capture average acceleration per day and time spent in MVPA. However, with the modern interest in sedentary behaviour and compositional analysis, the 7-day protocol is out-dated. It simply is not sufficient to capture all the behaviours we are interested in.
>
> On a related note - I am currently working on a project to modify this functionality a little bit such that if you really want you can include the 7th day. This may be useful for studies in children where we can assume a bit more safely that they fall a sleep before midnight. However, I will urge users to be careful with this as it is far from ideal and will make sure it is not a default setting.
>

I see two solutions:
Merge GGIR part 1 milestone data files (.RData in meta/basic folder) by appending the M$metalong and M$metashort objects inside it, impute the timegaps, and then run GGIR part 2 as you normally would.
Enhance GGIR to ease the process of merging recordings

Option 1 is probably best done as an R script, which does not require a very high level of R skills.

Option 2 requires a clear understanding of GGIR and I guess it makes sense if I am involved in that.

I'd be happy to do either of these a paid consultancy after the summer (quite busy at the moment). Direct message me if you are interested. Alternatively, you may be able to do option 1 yourself or someone with R skills in your environment.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent and group members,

I wonder whether this has now been updated in the newest version? (I think so 😊)
May I ask for some advice, please!

I am currently analyzing a similar short dataset (Geneactiv lab study, measurement duration: 2h) and thus would like to use 1s epoch ENMO data from part 1/2 only. The code works fine although, interestingly, I get two different days in the part2_daysummary.csv (Friday 1.75h and Saturday 0.25h). This seems to depend on the window sizes for the non-wear detection (I reduced them also) and perhaps more? But I am not sure why there are always two days...

Anyway, my main question is about using free-living calibration coefficients for the lab study (I would like to follow Hildebrand et al 2016). We have free-living data from the same device collected before/after the lab session. I have extracted the coefficients (x.scale etc.) from the free-living file “data_quality_report” and put them into a new file, which I have added to the code for the lab study (backup.cal.coef = location of new file).

I think, it worked (eg, angles/ENMO values are different between the analysis with and without “backup calibration” + no errors in R) but I am just not sure here:

1)      In general, am I right using the calibration values (x.scale etc.) from the “data quality report file” from the free-living measurements for that? Is this currently the best way to calibrate very short measurements in GGIR?

2)      When referring to the “old” free-living coefficients using “backup.cal.coef “, the angles/ENMOs are the same, irrespective of do.cal = TRUE/FALSE. I read it should be “FALSE” in a different post?

3)      I can find the “old" free-living cal. coefficients in the newly generated file “Data_quality_report” for the lab study but values of Zero for pre and post calibration error and the message saying “Autocalibration not done”. I guess this is ok since I manually calibrated them?

Further details:

When analyzing the lab study in the standard way (without backup cal.), calibration is done but auto-calibration not? Eg, there are values for cal.error.start = 0.01324, n.10sec.windows=216 but it tells me that recalibration was not done because there not enough points on all sided of the sphere. That is why I wondered about manual calibration.

Thank you very much!!

Best wishes

Matteo
